title: Theorem on formal functions over a complete Noetherian base ring
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal such that $A$ is $I$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism], $\mathcal I=I\mathcal O_X\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ the image of $f^*\widetilde I\to f^*\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\to\mathcal O_X$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal] (the ideal sheaf generated by the images of the elements of $I$), and $\mathcal F$ a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], with $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$ as in [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0). For $p\ge0$ the quotient maps $\mathcal F\to\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$ induce $A$-linear maps $H^p(X,\mathcal F)\to H^p(X,\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)$ [pqf-def-cohomology] compatible with the maps induced by $\mathcal F/\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F\to\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$. Then the induced map $$H^p(X,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow\varprojlim_nH^p(X,\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)$$ is an isomorphism of $A$-modules for every $p\ge0$; in particular ($p=0$) $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)\to\varprojlim_n\Gamma(X,\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)$ is bijective.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 087U (lemma-spell-out-theorem-formal-functions, line 5698); its proof: Theorem 02OC (theorem-formal-functions, line 5648), Lemma 02O6 (lemma-proper-over-affine-cohomology-finite: H^p finite over A) and Algebra, Lemma 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor: finite modules over a complete Noetherian ring are complete)

proof.text: (Finiteness.) Fix $p\ge0$ and put $H=H^p(X,\mathcal F)$, an $A$-module. Since $A$ is Noetherian, $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is proper and $\mathcal F$ is coherent, $H$ is a finite (finitely generated) $A$-module [lem-pc-coherent-hi] (Stacks 02O6, the case $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of that node).

proof.text: (Completeness of $H$.) $A$ is Noetherian and $I$-adically complete and $H$ is a finite $A$-module (step 1), so $H$ is $I$-adically complete [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-complete-over-complete-noetherian]: the canonical map $c:H\to H^\wedge=\varprojlim_nH/I^nH$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], $x\mapsto(x\bmod I^nH)_n$, is an $A$-linear bijection.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 087U (lemma-spell-out-theorem-formal-functions, line 5698): 'hence I-adically complete (Algebra, Lemma 00MA, lemma-completion-tensor)'; 00MA(3) with A -> A^ bijective

proof.text: (Theorem on formal functions.) By the theorem on formal functions [lem-weil-pbc-theorem-formal-functions] for the same $A$, $I$, $f$, $\mathcal F$, $\mathcal I=I\mathcal O_X$ and $p$ (its hypotheses are among ours: $A$ Noetherian, $f$ proper, $\mathcal F$ coherent), the maps $\theta_n:H/I^nH\to H^p(X,\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)$, $x\bmod I^nH\mapsto$ the image of $x$ under the map induced by $\mathcal F\to\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$, induce an isomorphism of $A$-modules $\theta=\varprojlim_n\theta_n:H^\wedge\to\varprojlim_nH^p(X,\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Theorem 02OC (theorem-formal-functions, line 5648), cited in the proof of Lemma 087U as 'a reformulation of the theorem on formal functions'

proof.text: (The map of the statement is $\theta\circ c$.) Let $\rho:H\to\varprojlim_nH^p(X,\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)$ be the map of the statement, $\rho(x)=(\rho_n(x))_n$ with $\rho_n:H\to H^p(X,\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)$ induced by the quotient map. For $x\in H$, $\theta(c(x))=(\theta_n(x\bmod I^nH))_n=(\rho_n(x))_n=\rho(x)$ by the definition of $\theta_n$ in step 3. So $\rho=\theta\circ c$ is a composite of two $A$-linear bijections (steps 2 and 3), hence an isomorphism of $A$-modules. This holds for every $p\ge0$; for $p=0$, $H^0(X,-)=\Gamma(X,-)$ [pqf-def-cohomology], which gives the last assertion.
